subject.title: Heartbeat: Use ISO 8601 for Current time and separate trigger timestamp

question: Should OpenClaw change the shared cron-style timestamp contract to ISO 8601 and add a model-visible heartbeat trigger timestamp, or fold heartbeat time semantics into the broader prompt-cache timestamp redesign?
rationale: The requested behavior changes shared prompt semantics across multiple agent paths and exposes wake timing that is currently an internal coalescing detail.

options.title: Define shared timestamp contract
options.body: Choose exact `Current time`, `Reference UTC`, and optional `Heartbeat triggered at` semantics across heartbeat, cron, reset, post-compaction, memory-flush, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Limit to heartbeat
options.body: Add heartbeat-only ISO formatting and trigger-time plumbing while leaving other shared helper callers on the current prompt shape.

options.title: Fold into prompt-cache redesign
options.body: Track this under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71973 so wall-clock placement and cache-boundary behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Define shared timestamp contract
recommendation.body: Choose exact `Current time`, `Reference UTC`, and optional `Heartbeat triggered at` semantics across heartbeat, cron, reset, post-compaction, memory-flush, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman introduced the heartbeat current-time helper path and is the strongest history-backed routing candidate for the timestamp contract decision.
